reuse.why: The averages reuse setNMonthAvg and the new action shares traversal, but copyPreviousMonth bypasses shared category selection and getFixedGroupIds reinvents existing tag helpers.

duplication.why: Average-action duplication is reduced, but category eligibility remains split between two paths, income eligibility is repeated, and tag recognition duplicates shared functionality.

placement.why: Budget policy and handler registration fit their existing layers, although tag interpretation belongs with the shared tag utilities.

scope.why: The edits stay focused on the requested month-wide actions, their registration, tests, and release note.

maintainability.why: The shared argument type and average wrappers improve ownership, but maintainers must still update multiple eligibility implementations when exclusions change.

bypasses_abstraction.where: actions.ts: copyPreviousMonth bypasses getMonthWideCategories, setZero repeats forEachMonthWideCategory's income gate, and getFixedGroupIds bypasses shared/tags.ts.

disguised_duplication.where: actions.ts: copyPreviousMonth spreads the shared selector's eligibility policy across getBudgetData SQL and callback guards, reshaping rather than consolidating the same decision.

abstraction_drift.where: actions.ts: includeHiddenCategories adds one selection parameter and conditional branch; copyPreviousMonth bypasses shared selection, while setZero bypasses shared traversal and retains its own income eligibility check.
